title: Se fue la luz
desc: The power goes and nobody reacts

sn.s: Son las ocho de la noche.
sn.e: It is eight at night.
I am in my room.
The fan is turning.
The light is on.
Suddenly everything goes off.
The light goes off.
The fan goes off.

sn.s: Se apagan las luces de toda la calle.
sn.e: The lights of the whole street go off.

sn.s: Se apaga la música del vecino.
sn.e: The neighbour's music goes off.
The room goes dark.
Everything goes dark.
I cannot see anything.
I wait a moment.
The light does not come back.

sn.s: Salgo del cuarto en lo oscuro.
sn.e: I leave the room in the dark.
The whole house is dark.
I go towards the door.
Outside it is dark too.
The whole street is dark.
All the houses are dark.
I think it is something serious.
But the people are calm.

sn.s: Doña Carmen sale con una vela.
sn.e: Doña Carmen comes out with a candle.

sn.s: Prende la vela con un fósforo.
sn.e: She lights the candle with a match.

sn.s: Pone la vela en la mesa.
sn.e: She puts the candle on the table.

sn.s: Prende otra vela para la cocina.
sn.e: She lights another candle for the kitchen.
"What happened?" I ask.

sn.s: "Se fue la luz", dice doña Carmen.
sn.e: "The power went," doña Carmen says.
She says it calmly.
As if it were nothing.
"And when does it come back?" I ask.
"It comes back when it comes back," she says.

sn.s: Roberto saca dos sillas a la calle.
sn.e: Roberto takes two chairs out to the street.
He takes out one chair for himself.

sn.s: Saca una silla para su mamá.
sn.e: He takes out one chair for his mum.
Then he takes out one more chair.

sn.s: "Esta silla es para vos", me dice.
sn.e: "This chair is for you," he says to me.

sn.s: Es la primera vez que me dice vos.
sn.e: It is the first time he says vos to me.

sn.s: Nos sentamos afuera en las sillas.
sn.e: We sit outside on the chairs.
The neighbours take out chairs too.
The whole street is outside.

sn.s: Adentro de las casas hace más calor.
sn.e: It is hotter inside the houses.

sn.s: Sin abanico, adentro no se puede estar.
sn.e: Without a fan you cannot stay inside.

sn.s: Afuera corre un poco de aire.
sn.e: Outside there is a bit of a breeze.

sn.s: La gente habla de una casa a otra.
sn.e: People talk from one house to another.
Nobody talks about the power.
They talk about other things.
They talk about the heat.
They talk about food.
A man talks about baseball.

sn.s: Yo escucho y no entiendo todo.
sn.e: I listen and do not understand everything.
But I understand a little.

sn.s: Cada día entiendo un poco más.
sn.e: Every day I understand a little more.

sn.s: Las velas se ven en todas las puertas.
sn.e: Candles can be seen in every doorway.

sn.s: La calle está oscura y llena de gente.
sn.e: The street is dark and full of people.
Two hours go by.
Nobody complains.
Nobody calls anyone.
They just wait.
I wait with them.
Suddenly the power comes back.

sn.s: Se prenden las luces de la calle.
sn.e: The street lights come on.
The fans come on.

sn.s: En las casas suena la música otra vez.
sn.e: Music starts again in the houses.

sn.s: La gente dice "¡ah!" y se ríe.
sn.e: People say "ah!" and laugh.

sn.s: Roberto apaga la vela con la mano.
sn.e: Roberto puts out the candle with his hand.

sn.s: Doña Carmen apaga la otra vela.
sn.e: Doña Carmen puts out the other candle.

sn.s: Los vecinos apagan sus velas también.
sn.e: The neighbours put out their candles too.

sn.s: Nadie apaga el abanico esa noche.
sn.e: Nobody turns off the fan that night.

sn.s: Uno no apaga el abanico nunca.
sn.e: You never turn off the fan.

sn.s: Todos meten las sillas a las casas.
sn.e: Everyone takes the chairs back into the houses.

sn.s: En cinco minutos la calle está vacía.
sn.e: In five minutes the street is empty.
I go back to my room.
I turn the fan on again.

sn.s: Pienso en las dos horas afuera.
sn.e: I think about the two hours outside.

sn.s: Se fue la luz y nadie se enojó.
sn.e: The power went and nobody got angry.

sn.s: Se fue la luz y la calle se llenó de gente.
sn.e: The power went and the street filled with people.

sn.s: En mi país eso sería un problema.
sn.e: In my country that would be a problem.
Here it is an ordinary night.
